todos.note: learn-from-the-test.md:180's Meta bullet still misdescribes the M5 cross-cwd boundary: 'M5 forks a worktree at `../<repo-name>-m5` and the packaged re-send runs in a fresh session there (cross-cwd boundary, so `new`, not the same session as diagnose + build + assemble)'. Read against the actual mechanics — `exercises/fork-the-worktree.md:5` runs the fork in the ORIGINAL repo; `exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md:5` opens 'Session (new, "Module 5 worktree session")' already IN the worktree; the re-send at `exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md:111` is 'Session (new, "M5 long-run")', also in the worktree (a fresh session for a clean context window per L119, not a cwd change) — the actual cross-cwd boundary is the earlier fork step (original repo -> worktree), not the diagnose-to-resend step, which is same-cwd/new-session. This was filed as a todo against the prior audit (pre-2026-09-02) and is unchanged in the current body (only the `<repo>-m5` -> `<repo-name>-m5` token was renamed, consistently and correctly, across every file this session checked). Not a rule violation — the student-facing Session widgets in both exercises are unambiguous and independently verified PASS on rule 4 — but the trainer-only Meta prose still misdescribes which step is the cwd change, and is worth a correction pass.
